definition: Forthright means direct and honest in what one says.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word forthright. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know forthright should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The estimate was forthright: the mason listed what the wall would cost, what could go wrong, and which repairs could safely wait a decade.
Direct is milder than forthright — direct only promises no detours, while forthright adds honesty that may cost the speaker something.
Tactless goes further than forthright and falls off the good end of the ladder: the forthright speaker tells hard truths with care, while the tactless one tramples feelings without noticing.

Plainspoken is a habit of style — plain, everyday words with no jargon or ornament. Forthright is about substance: a forthright answer tells the hard truth even when the truth costs the speaker, and it can arrive in fancy language. A plainspoken person may still dodge the hard question.

Outspoken people voice their opinions freely and unprompted, sometimes more often and more loudly than anyone asked. Forthright is narrower: it means answering what you are asked directly and honestly. The outspoken volunteer their views; the forthright deliver the truth a question was owed.
